name: sensitivity-uq
title: Global sensitivity: which enzyme capacities drive the glycolysis model?
question:
Across the glycolysis model's enzyme-capacity (Vmax) parameters, which ones
actually drive the output (steady-state ATP), and by how much — a global
sensitivity screen rather than a one-at-a-time local derivative?
hypothesis:
A small number of parameters dominate the flux: classical control analysis puts
glucose transport and hexokinase near the top. A Morris elementary-effects screen
over all Vmax parameters should produce a sharply discriminating importance
ranking (one or two parameters far above the median), not a flat one.
objective:
Run a seeded Morris elementary-effects screen (r trajectories, ±20% around each
nominal Vmax) over the glycolysis Vmax parameters on the Ray ensemble, with
steady-state ATP as the quantity of interest; report mu* (importance) and sigma
(interaction / nonlinearity) and the ranking; grade that the ranking discriminates.
description:
Sensitivity / UQ study for the SBML-decomposition investigation. The sensitivity
harness (viva_sbml_decomposition.harness.sensitivity) builds a seeded Morris
design over the 14 Vmax parameters (±20% around nominal, a biologically
reasonable and numerically stable range — wider ranges push glycolysis out of its
stable regime) and evaluates the samples in parallel through the ensemble
(run_ensemble; serial fallback). The quantity of interest is steady-state ATP,
which responds clearly to the Vmax sweep.

Morris on the deterministic ODE is REPRODUCIBLE given the seed, so the verdict
grades the ranking's discrimination (top mu* vs median), not raw magnitudes
(which vary in their last digits across BLAS/platforms). The committed baseline
(visualizations/sensitivity_indices.json) is this machine's mu*/sigma. The
measured ranking is strongly discriminating — glucose transport (vGLT) dominates,
then glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (vG3PDH) and hexokinase (vGLK) —
the classical flux-controlling steps, consistent with the hypothesis.

expected_behavior.name: sensitivity-ranking-discriminates
expected_behavior.observable: Morris mu* (importance) per Vmax parameter for steady-state ATP, and the top/median ratio
expected_behavior.condition: the ranking discriminates — the most important parameter's mu* is at least 3x the median (a degenerate, unresponsive QoI would be ~1x); indices finite and reproducible given the seed
expected_behavior.rationale: a useful global sensitivity analysis must separate the flux-controlling parameters from the rest; a flat ranking means the QoI or range was poorly chosen.

readouts.name: sensitivity_indices
readouts.description: Machine-tagged Morris indices — mu* (importance) and sigma (interaction/nonlinearity) per Vmax parameter, and the ranking.

behavior_tests.name: sensitivity-ranking-discriminates

pass_if.detail: top mu* >= 3x median mu* (ranking discriminates), indices finite
